Story: Seraiah Casts the Book into the Euphrates
Retelling: The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah the son of Neriah, when he went with Zedekiah the king of Judah into Babylon in the fourth year of his reign — Seraiah was a quiet prince. Jeremiah had written in a book all the evil that should come upon Babylon, even all these words that are written against Babylon. And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, When thou comest to Babylon, and shalt see, and shalt read all these words, then shalt thou say, O LORD, Thou hast spoken against this place, to cut it off, that none shall remain in it, neither man nor beast, but that it shall be desolate for ever. And it shall be, when thou hast made an end of reading this book, that thou shalt bind a stone to it, and cast it into the midst of Euphrates, and shalt say, Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise from the evil that I will bring upon her, and they shall be weary.
Discussion: A book and a stone, thrown into a river, preached the fall of an empire. Reflect: 1) Why send Babylon's judgment by a quiet prince on a royal journey, rather than by an army? 2) How does a sinking stone preach what a thousand words cannot? 3) What does it mean that Babylon's fall was already written before Babylon itself had fallen?
Significance: Babylon, the power that carried Judah away, would itself sink like a stone-bound book in the Euphrates and not rise again. Doubt: this is a prophetic sign-act, a staged picture or lived sign, rather than an ordinary historical episode.
